notes:
I couldn't write any notes on Psalm 45 this time, because my research tool stopped working before I could open a single page. My first attempt to fetch the sources failed, and so did a retry, both with an error saying I had no tool calls left. I didn't read Enduring Word, Bible Hub, StudyLight, NET Bible, New Advent or any of the other approved sites.

Your rules say to report only what the pages actually say, cite a URL for every point, and never fill gaps from my own knowledge. Without any pages read, I have nothing I can honestly put in the notes. I could write a commentary from memory, but that would break those rules and leave you with unchecked claims and no real links, so I haven't.

If you ask again in a new message, the tool should be available, and I'll start with these pages:

- **Traditional reading, verse by verse:** Enduring Word on Psalm 45; Gill, Ellicott and the Pulpit Commentary on Bible Hub; Spurgeon's *Treasury of David*; Precept Austin.
- **Where Protestant traditions differ:** mainly vv. 6–7 (quoted in Hebrews 1:8–9) and the bride and queen in vv. 9–15. Sources would be Reformed (Ligonier, Monergism, The Gospel Coalition), Baptist (Spurgeon.org, Desiring God, GTY), Wesley's notes on wesley.nnu.edu, and Lutheran (LCMS, 1517).
- **Other views:**
  - **Modern scholarship:** the NET Bible notes on how to translate "Your throne, O God" in v. 6, and Bible Odyssey on royal wedding psalms.
  - **Catholic and Orthodox:** Augustine on this psalm (numbered Psalm 44 in his Latin Bible) on New Advent; Catholic.com and OCA on the queen and the Virgin Mary in v. 9.
  - **Popular modern teaching:** only if the approved sites actually discuss it in connection with this psalm.

You could also paste in the text of particular commentary pages, and I'll write the notes straight from those.
